subject: Post-demo: TTFT & streaming cadence qualification (latency / concurrency plan)
messages:
From: Sophie Wang <sophie.wang@fastbank.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: DevOps <infra@fastbank.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Feb 2026 15:10:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Discovery call recap — TTFT & streaming expectations

Thanks for the demo earlier today — nice walkthrough. A couple quick clarifications as we internalize the requirements:  

- Target for Time-to-First-Token (TTFT): ideally under 150 ms p95 for our web chat flows, but we can tolerate up to 200 ms p95 on peak if throughput is preserved.  
- Streaming: prefer SSE to start (simpler client integration), but will need WebSocket option later for lower-latency agent UI. Chunk cadence: we expect chunks every ~80–120 ms on average when streaming long responses; good to know if Redwood can tune chunk sizes vs cadence.  
- Throughput / concurrency: our baseline is ~300 RPS with bursts to 1k RPS during spikes; average tokens per response ~90. We care about steady-state latency and graceful degradation if concurrency increases.  

Next step for us: can you send a concise qualification plan with measurable SLOs and a load-testing cadence we can sync on? Also include any recommended model variants (quantized vs FP16) you expect will meet the TTFT target.

Thanks,
Sophie
Lead PM, Conversational Experience
FastBank

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Sophie Wang <sophie.wang@fastbank.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 18 Feb 2026 17:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Discovery call recap — TTFT & streaming expectations

Hi Sophie — great to talk. Appreciate the clarity on targets. High-level confirmation below and an ask for one piece of infra info from your DevOps team (see inline). I attached a short plan (redwood-ttft-cadence-proposal.pdf) and a load plan template for your infra team.

Recap / proposed measurable SLOs:  
- TTFT (user-facing): p95 <= 150 ms for chat UI (web SSE) during baseline (<= 300 RPS). Escalation SLO: p95 <= 200 ms during brief bursts up to 1k RPS; we will model headroom using burst capacity.
- Streaming cadence: initial recommendation SSE with chunk cadence target 60–100 ms between chunks for long-form responses. If you need sub-60ms cadence, we recommend WebSocket with our low-latency routing (may increase infra cost).
- Throughput & concurrency: aim to validate 350 RPS sustained with concurrency ~= 64 concurrent in-flight requests per worker. We'll size horizontally; exact instance counts depend on model and quantization.
- Model options: 1) quantized 4-bit variant (best cost/latency trade) for baseline; 2) FP16 for strict quality-first flows (higher infra).

DevOps ask (DevOps contact cc'd): can you confirm whether FastBank will allow outbound TLS to our staging endpoints and provide a 24-hour test window for load testing (preferred times: Tue / Thu 02:00–06:00 UTC)? We need a sandbox credential set + approximate NAT IPs to allowlist.

Next steps (proposed):  
1) Your DevOps confirms allowlist and test window (fastbank infra).  
2) Redwood runs a 4-hour load test against your staging with the quantized model and SSE streaming; we'll produce a p50/p95/p99 breakdown and chunk cadence histogram.  
3) Review results and iterate: if TTFT > target, we test FP16 + dedicated capacity and measure KV cache warmup behavior.

I've attached the short plan and load template. Marcus / Laura — can you pick owners for the test run and pick an initial staging configuration (GPU type / per-worker concurrency)?

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Attachments:
- redwood-ttft-cadence-proposal.pdf (1.2MB)
- slo-load-plan.xlsx (staging-load-plan template)

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Sophie Wang <sophie.wang@fastbank.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>, DevOps <infra@fastbank.com>
Date: Thu, 19 Feb 2026 09:13:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Discovery call recap — TTFT & streaming expectations

Adding some engineering detail from the SRE/SE side so expectations are explicit. We're proposing the following concrete test configuration for the initial run:  

- Model: "open-instruct-xl" quantized (bitsandbytes 4-bit). Baseline token output profile: 60–120 tokens per response.  
- Serving mode: SSE streaming, default chunking logic set to emit chunks ~64 tokens or every 75ms (whichever comes first). We'll capture actual cadence in histograms.  
- Worker instance: 1x A100-80GB per worker for the quantized config; conservative concurrency per worker: 64 in-flight requests. Expect per-worker p95 TTFT ~ 110–160 ms depending on prefix length.  
- Throughput target for test: ramp to 350 RPS sustained for 1 hour, then 1,000 RPS spike test for 10 minutes to validate graceful degradation and fallback.  
- KV cache warmup: include a short warmup phase (10 minutes) to ensure common prompts hit prefix cache; we'll record cold vs warm TTFT.  

Measurement/outputs we'll share: p50/p95/p99 TTFT; chunk cadence CDF; tokens/sec delivered; error rate; CPU/GPU utilization traces (per-worker); and system-level latencies (LB, network). If SSE cadence shows >120ms median gaps, we'll propose WebSocket and smaller chunk thresholds.  

Sophie / FastBank infra: please confirm the test window and allowlist. Also indicate whether you want us to run the spike test against the same staging endpoint or a separate canary to isolate impact.

I'll own the run. Laura will help analyze chunk cadence histograms and propose chunk-size tuning.

- Marcus
Principal Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

From: Sophie Wang <sophie.wang@fastbank.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>, DevOps <infra@fastbank.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Feb 2026 11:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Discovery call recap — TTFT & streaming expectations

Thanks — this looks good and very aligned with what we discussed. Quick confirmations:  

- FastBank approves the 4-hour window on Tue 24 Feb 02:00–06:00 UTC for the initial load run. We'll provide a sandbox credential and NAT IPs by EOD Mon (23 Feb).  
- Please run the spike test against a separate canary endpoint (we'll split traffic to production later).  
- We prefer you start with SSE and include an additional WebSocket run only if SSE cannot meet cadence requirements (per your analysis).

Sophie
Lead PM, Conversational Experience
FastBank
